paper.abstract_en: Electromagnetic properties of materials are commonly inferred from how they scatter light. Here we show that this diagnostic is fundamentally incomplete. We predict the existence of an intrinsic electromagnetic property that remains invisible in any scattering experiment independently of geometry, polarization, far-field or near-field excitation. Still, this property affects the radiation emitted by the sources embedded inside the material. We reveal this phenomenon for a specially designed nonreciprocal magnetoelectric material combining axion and dual axion responses. Our results establish intrinsic electromagnetic properties as a distinct class of material responses and show that scattering experiments alone are insufficient to characterize matter.
